title: Orchard bridge log and deferred playbook - 2026-09-29
content:
Shift window: 2026-09-29 03:00 - 11:00 PT (EU overlap).
Owner on shift: Evelyn Park (primary), Mateo Alvarez (backup)
Channels: #sre-ops (primary), #prod-alerts, PagerDuty PDINC-20260929-01

Executive summary:
- Tonight we observed a multi-modal latency uptick affecting hosted-api routes for mid-sized chat workloads between 04:10-05:50 PT. Peak p95 increased from baseline ~220ms to ~1.2s for ~45 minutes, with intermittent 5xx errors on model-serving proxies. Impacted customers: small subset of hosted API customers; no Dedicated clusters.
- Immediate mitigation: scaled up model-router pool, activated short-circuit fallback to smaller-quant variant for high-latency requests, and tightened batching window to reduce head-of-line queuing. Those actions recovered p95 to ~300ms by 05:30 PT.
- Root-cause (initial hypothesis): transient kernel scheduling interaction on a subset of GPU hosts combined with a mis-tuned autoscaler threshold for model-router pods. There is a secondary hypothesis around cache invalidation causing re-warm on KV caches for long-chained conversations.

Timeline (high-level):
- 04:06 PT: Alert triggered - sustained p95 > 650ms on hosted-api (route: /v1/streams/generate-chat).
- 04:10 PT: PagerDuty fired. I joined bridge and triaged. Observed correlated increase in CPU steal and occasional OOMKilled kube-proxy restarts on 3 hosts in us-west2-a.
- 04:18 PT: Confirmed customer-facing 502/504 spikes. Opened SRE incident PDINC-20260929-01.
- 04:25 PT: Began rolling a manual scaler bump for model-router deployment from min=6 -> min=12 in us-west2-a to drain queuing.
- 04:40 PT: Identified pattern: affected hosts share older NVIDIA driver (510.x) vs fleet baseline 535.x; one recent kernel patch had been applied earlier this week (hostpool auto-updates).
- 04:48 PT: Activated fallback policy to model-quant-small variant for ~8% traffic to reduce per-token compute.
- 05:05 PT: Error rate dropped but p95 still elevated. Ran targeted pod restarts for kube-proxy on two hosts; observed CPU-steal drop.
- 05:22 PT: p95 back to ~300ms; 5xx events stabilized below alert threshold.
- 05:50 PT: Declared major mode transition complete; downgraded PagerDuty to watch.
- 07:00 PT: Post-incident pass: observed a small recurrence (05:50-06:05 PT equivalent) likely tied to autoscaler policy still being conservative; we adjusted thresholds and placed a temporary override to prefer headroom.

What we changed (operational actions taken):
- Manual autoscaler min increased for model-router in us-west2-a (reverted to previous after stabilization; follow-up to automate policy change if patterns repeat).
- Short-circuit routing: routed 8% of cross-traffic to quant-small model variant (temporary override, removed at 06:10 PT).
- Pod restarts: restarted kube-proxy on nodes i-0a12b3c4d (2 nodes) after confirming restarts correlated with CPU steal improvements.
- Created incident ticket SRE-3421 to track rollout of driver baseline standardization across the pool.

Customer impact summary:
- Affected set: ~2.1% of hosted API requests during window; primarily customers with long chat context (>=4k tokens).
- Visible behavior: delayed streaming starts, intermittent 502/504 at peaks. No data loss observed. We proactively notified customer success for two enterprise customers (CS case #12084, #12085) who reported degraded UX.

Follow-ups (requires owners and SLA):
- Driver standardization across fleet (owner: infra-team / Mateo Alvarez) — create gated rollout plan for kernel/driver sync and canary windows (target: SRE-3421). Due: 2026-10-06.
- Autoscaler policy tuning (owner: serving-runtime / Rina Sato) — instrument autoscaler with more granular queue depth metrics and add predictive headroom based on sliding-window latency. Due: 2026-10-03.
- KV cache warmup audit (owner: applied-ml / Jordan Lee) — verify cache invalidation patterns for long conversations and add a synthetic warmup during scale-ups. Due: 2026-10-01.
- Runbook patch: add explicit checklist for "GPU host driver mismatch" path including telemetry queries and rollback steps (owner: eng-sre / Evelyn Park). Due: 2026-09-30.
- Customer outreach log: CS cases updated and initial outreach sent; CS to provide follow-up status (owner: customer-success). Due: 2026-09-30.

Notes for next shift / Handoff items:
- Monitor us-west2-a hostpool for pending auto-updates; infra has temporarily paused autoroll for that pool pending SRE review.
- Watch for recurring p95 spikes if predictive autoscaler is engaged during business hours; throttle automatic scale-down for next 48h.
- If similar symptoms occur: 1) check kernel/driver baseline across affected nodes, 2) confirm kube-proxy health, 3) apply short-lived quant routing to 5-10% and raise autoscaler min as emergency measure. Add this as a quick-play in runbook.
- Link to ad-hoc Grafana panel: https://grafana.redwood.internal/d/ops/latency-orchard-2026-09-29

Runbook gaps observed (suggested edits):
- Current runbook lacks clear signal thresholds for when to route to quant variants — add numeric thresholds (p95 > 600ms for 5m).
- No step to check driver/kernel version parity across hostpool — add CLI commands and recommended query to fleet index.
- Autoscaler guidance too generic; include explicit safe-min values by region and load-class.

Temporary playbook snippet to be inserted into runbook (for quick copy):
- Trigger condition: p95 > 600ms sustained > 5m with >0.5% 5xx increase.
- Immediate mitigations: 1) bump model-router min replicas +30% in affected region, 2) route 5-10% to quant-small variant, 3) restart kube-proxy on nodes with elevated CPU-steal after approval, 4) open PDINC and notify CS for customers with >1% traffic affected.

Deferred/low-priority items (not blocking):
- Instrumentation: add kernel-driver version to host telemetry and alert on drift (infra).
- Investigate whether a memory fragmentation pattern in the runtime allocators triggered cold-paths for long contexts (applied-ml).
- Consider a small perpetual canary traffic stream to exercise long-conversation paths in dedicated clusters (prod-ops).

Logs/Artifacts attached / helpful links:
- Grafana panel (ops): https://grafana.redwood.internal/d/ops/latency-orchard-2026-09-29
- PagerDuty: PDINC-20260929-01
- Confluence incident page: https://confluence.redwood.internal/display/SRE/latency-investigation-2026-09-29
- GitHub PR with temporary quant routing toggle: https://github.com/redwood-inference/runtime/pull/1876

Decision record / temporary policy changes made:
- Short-lived policy: prefer conservative autoscaler floor for hostpool us-west2-a for 48h. Change made at 05:15 PT and will be auto-reverted on 2026-10-01 unless SRE approves extension.

Post-shift reflections (notes to self):
- Sequence of events felt like two orthogonal failures (host-level driver drift + autoscaler being too eager to scale-to-zero). We should not treat autoscaler as primary remediation without checking host parity.
- Communication: CS notification went out fast but could use templated wording for latency incidents to reduce manual edits. I'll draft one and attach to SRE-3421.

Immediate blockers for handoff: none. System stabilized and temporary mitigations removed except autoscaler conservative floor.

Signed off by: Evelyn Park (oncall), Mateo Alvarez (backup)

Quick checklist for incoming shift:
- Acknowledge this doc and PDINC in bridge.
- Confirm infra paused autoroll for us-west2-a (Slack @infra).
- Watch p95 and 5xx for next 6 hours.
- Ensure follow-ups have assignees (see SRE-3421 and linked Confluence).

-- end of shift notes --
